title: RuleDetonate
summary: A pre-load checker for AI coding-agent rule files that flags injected dependency redirection.
meta: Telkom University · benchmark dataset on Kaggle

card.caption: detected at 5% FPR, vs 7.8% for the best baseline

kpis.label: detected at a 5% false-positive rate, against at most 7.8% for general detectors
detected at a 10% false-positive rate, against 14.1%
stages, from sentence classifier to fusion

credit: Co-authored with Keanu Fibie Dimasyqi and Muhammad Fanny Adinata

goal: Detect injected sentences in AI coding-agent rule files that redirect the agent to an attacker-controlled package, before the agent loads the file.
setup: Four stages: a DeBERTa-v3-small sentence classifier with package names masked, a counterfactual test with a surrogate agent (Qwen2.5-Coder-14B, 4-bit), package evidence (name proximity, registry trust, age, release count, known vulnerabilities) and a logistic-regression fusion.

Evaluated on a strict subset of 256 redirected and 239 benign files against ProtectAI, deepset, PIGuard, Prompt Guard 2, a PIShield-style probe, a regex, an allowlist and an LLM judge, all compared at the same false-positive rate.
did: The checker runs before the agent loads a rule file and works in four stages: a DeBERTa-v3-small sentence classifier, a counterfactual test with a surrogate coding agent (Qwen2.5-Coder-14B), package-level evidence, and a logistic-regression fusion.
results: At 5% FPR it detects 26.2% of redirected files, against at most 7.8% for general-purpose prompt-injection detectors. At 10% FPR the figures are 32.8% and 14.1%.
On the fresh cohort, whose authors and package names were never used for tuning: 17.5% at 5% FPR, against at most 10.4%.
Paired ablation: removing the sentence classifier raises the false-negative rate by 0.303, package evidence by 0.090 and the agent probe by 0.050.
On 40 pairs of real rule files the fused detector flags injected files more often than their originals (McNemar p = 0.0039).

General prompt-injection detectors miss hidden dependency manipulation in AI coding-agent config files. A counterfactual test with a surrogate model plus OSV package checks gives a measured first layer before the agent runs.
failed: About three quarters of redirected files still go undetected at 5% FPR.
All attacks are synthetic, and the real-file set is small (92 pairs, 40 through the full pipeline) and comes from one source.
The surrogate-agent probe adds the least while costing the most. Line attribution was not evaluated, and attackers who age their packages were not tested.
next: Test attacks optimized against the checker, and attackers who age their packages.
Collect rule files from other sources and formats.
Measure end-to-end attack success in a live agent loop.
Look for a cheaper alternative to the surrogate-agent stage.
